correctness.rationale: Subtracting the hub output gives a continuous piecewise linear map on the nonnegative cone. The input modulus map is Euclidean nonexpansive. With a global-mean hub, leaf edge rows are zero or restrictions of I−11ᵀ/(m+1), so the norm is at most one. With a singleton hub, let I_i=e_i−e_0 and H=ΣI_i/(m+1). The rows are I_i, I_i/2 or H; at least one row is not I_i by the strict mean inequality. Their nonnegative Gram matrix is dominated entrywise by replacing all half rows by H, then all but one H by the corresponding I_i. The symmetric block has trace m(m+2)/(m+1), determinant 1/(m+1), and top eigenvalue exceeding one, with remaining contrast eigenvalue one where present. Segment decomposition and continuity handle all pairs including ties. For m≥2 the witness hub 2, m−1 leaves of value 2+1/(4m), and last leaf 1 has 3/2<a<2 and realizes the maximizing rows strictly. With λ the top eigenvalue, the left eigenvector with first m−1 entries 1 and last λ−m yields an actual positive finite perturbation in its right singular direction. For m=1 the edge difference is (x_1−x_0)/2 on the modulus cone, so the squared Euclidean norm is 1/2. The trace and determinant also give λ/m→1.
residual_risks: Uploaded floating-point checks were not executed; the finite-pair and all-degree assertions were checked analytically.

value.rationale: Exact finite-degree perturbation constants for a natural family separate one-input edge smoothing from potentially large two-input edge responses. The result identifies the strict feasible maximizer and the mechanism by which a single global-average row and many singleton rows produce the sharp value, rather than only a norm-conversion or growth estimate.
